draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Nelliyampathy! Hills of tea, coffee and orange groves rise above the plains here, about 1,500 metres at the top. The road up from Nenmara has ten hairpin bends.
draft.hungryLine: Food up here is simple estate fare. Carry snacks and eat at the few local eateries.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Stop at Pothundi Dam on the way up, then head to Seetharkundu viewpoint.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stand at Seetharkundu and look down at the plains of Palakkad spread out below.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Seetharkundu is named after Sita. Legend says she bathed in the stream here during her exile.

spots.name: Seetharkundu Viewpoint
spots.detail: Short drive · A sheer drop with a view

spots.name: Pothundi Dam
spots.detail: At the foot of the hills · A reservoir

legends.title: Sita's pool
legends.body: Legend says Sita, Rama and Lakshmana stopped here during their exile, and Sita bathed in the stream.

legends.title: Oranges in Kerala
legends.body: Nelliyampathy is one of the few places in Kerala where oranges grow.

tips.title: Go up in the morning.
tips.body: Clouds often hide the views by afternoon.

tips.title: Fuel up below.
tips.body: There are few petrol pumps in the hills.

story.title: Forest hills
story.body: These hills are part of the Western Ghats, home to elephants and hornbills.

story.title: Sita's stop
story.body: Legend links the stream at Seetharkundu to Sita's time in exile.

story.title: Estates arrive
story.body: Planters cleared the slopes for tea, coffee and oranges.

story.title: A quiet escape
story.body: Nelliyampathy stayed quieter than Munnar, loved by people who wanted calm.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Dam, hairpins, then Seetharkundu. Tell me if the plains looked like a map.
